To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the anorexia and weight loss that are associated with ageing are multifactorial; 2) they are associated with loss of muscle mass; 3) the loss of muscle mass can be treated by testosterone replacement in men; 4) the loss of skeletal muscle mass is associated with increased frailty and increased mortality; and 5) dieting in older individuals can lead to loss of skeletal muscle as well as adipose tissue and can lead to increased frailty and mortality
(i) the physiological anorectic system is intact in older individuals and that the anorectic effect of the physiological anorectics is enhanced in older individuals.
